name: Polycythemia Vera
remarks: Polycythemia Vera (PV) is a JAK2-mutated clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) characterised
by excessive erythrocytosis, often with concomitant leukocytosis and thrombocytosis.
EPIDEMIOLOGY
Incidence: 0.6-1.6 per 100,000 persons per year (US data).
Prevalence: ~44-57 per 100,000 (US).
Median age at diagnosis: ~65 years; rare below age 40.
Male:Female ratio approximately 1.2:1 (modelled via complex_transition).
Median overall survival >35 years in patients diagnosed <60 years.
DIAGNOSIS (WHO 2022 / ICC 2022 criteria)
Major criteria:
1. Hb >16.5 g/dL (men) or >16.0 g/dL (women), OR Hct >49% (men) / >48% (women)
2. Bone marrow biopsy: hypercellularity with trilineage panmyelosis and pleomorphic megakaryocytes
3. Presence of JAK2 V617F or JAK2 exon 12 mutation (>97% JAK2 V617F)
Minor criterion:
1. Subnormal serum erythropoietin (Epo) level
Diagnosis: all 3 major criteria OR major criteria 1+2 plus the minor criterion.
RISK STRATIFICATION (thrombotic risk)
Low-risk:  Age <60 years AND no prior thrombotic event
High-risk: Age >=60 years OR prior arterial/venous thrombosis
TREATMENT ALGORITHM
All patients: Phlebotomy (Hct target <45%) + aspirin 81 mg/day LIFELONG
NB: Aspirin stopped when systemic anticoagulation initiated (ECLAP bleeding data).
High-risk: Add cytoreductive therapy
First-line:  Hydroxyurea OR ropeginterferon alfa-2b (Besremi, FDA-approved 2021)
[peg-IFN alfa-2a used in this module as RxNorm proxy; off-label US]
Second-line: Ruxolitinib (HU-resistant/intolerant; FDA 2014) or Busulfan (elderly)
Symptomatic low-risk: cytoreduction per NCCN/ELN in ~20% of patients
Pruritus: paroxetine 20 mg/day (RxNorm 41493) or fluoxetine 20 mg/day (RxNorm 4493030)
Post-VTE: indefinite anticoagulation (warfarin); aspirin discontinued
DISEASE PROGRESSION
Post-PV MF:           ~10-20% at 20 years
AML transformation:   ~4-5%   at 20 years
Thrombotic events:    ~26%    at 20 years
Haemorrhagic events:  ~7-15%  lifetime

remarks: Bone marrow biopsy recommended for all newly diagnosed PV (WHO 2022/ICC 2022)
to confirm diagnosis and establish baseline fibrosis grade.
May be bypassed if Hb markedly elevated + JAK2 V617F confirmed.
~75% of patients undergo BMBx in practice.
SNOMED: 396487009 - Bone marrow biopsy.
Histology: hypercellular marrow, trilineage panmyelosis, pleomorphic megakaryocytes.
Baseline fibrosis: MF-0 or MF-1 in ~90% of newly diagnosed PV.
FIX 9: Bone marrow reticulin fibrosis grade (WHO/EUMNET).
LOINC: 85319-2 - Bone marrow Reticulin grade by WHO.
Scale: MF-0 (none) to MF-3 (dense collagen). Baseline PV: MF-0 or MF-1 (range 0-1).
Progression to MF-2/3 defines post-PV myelofibrosis.

Approximately one-third of PV patients develop clinically significant hyperuricaemia requiring allopurinol.

FIX 1: Aspirin is LIFELONG therapy - duration set to 50 years.
RxNorm: 1049502 - Aspirin 81 MG Oral Tablet.
Universal for all PV patients absent contraindications.
Contraindications: extreme thrombocytosis >1500e9/L, active bleeding, acquired vWD.
Reduces microvascular events and CVD (ECLAP trial, Landolfi 2004 NEJM).
FIX 2: Aspirin is ended (MedicationEnd state) when anticoagulation is initiated.
Concurrent aspirin + anticoagulation: major bleeding HR 5.83 (ECLAP data).

remarks: SNOMED: 67270000 - Phlebotomy.
Initial therapeutic phlebotomy: 450-500 mL per session.
Hct target <45% proven by CYTO-PV (Marchioli 2013 NEJM).
Initial frequency weekly until Hct <45%, then maintenance as needed.
Cytoreduction algorithm:
High-risk (age >=60 or thrombosis history): always cytoreduct.
Low-risk: ~20% receive cytoreduction for symptoms per NCCN/ELN.
Low-risk asymptomatic: phlebotomy + aspirin only.
FIX 11: ~20% of low-risk patients develop indication for cytoreduction:
Refractory pruritus, rising counts, frequent phlebotomy need, splenomegaly.
NCCN/ELN support this pathway for symptomatic low-risk disease.
FIX 10: Erythromelalgia modelled in ~8% of PV patients.
Burning pain and erythema of extremities from platelet-mediated microvascular occlusion.
Responds well to low-dose aspirin in most cases.
FIX 10: SNOMED: 271807003 - Erythromelalgia (disorder).
Characteristic of JAK2-mutated MPNs. Usually responds to aspirin.
Refractory cases may benefit from ruxolitinib.
First-line cytoreduction selection:
HU: preferred in patients >=50; most widely used globally.
Peg-IFN alfa-2a (proxy for ropeginterferon alfa-2b): preferred <50, reproductive-age women.
Real-world: ~70-75% HU first-line, ~25-30% interferon.
Under 50: 40% interferon, 60% HU.

Starting: 500-1000 mg/day; maintenance 500-2000 mg/day (titrated to CBC).
amount:2 frequency:1 = 1000 mg/day starting dose.

Resistance/intolerance: ~15-25% at 5 years (ELN 2011 criteria).
Adverse effects: cytopenias, leg ulcers, mucocutaneous toxicity, fever.
FIX 14: Ropeginterferon alfa-2b (Besremi) is FDA-approved Nov 2021 for PV
and is now the preferred interferon in current US guidelines (NCCN, ASH 2022).
RxNorm: 2281945 (ropeginterferon alfa-2b) should be substituted for US simulations.

Dose: 45-90 mcg SC weekly (peg-IFN alfa-2a); ropeg 100-250 mcg SC every 2 weeks.

remarks: RxNorm: 1049721 - Warfarin Sodium 5 MG Oral Tablet.
Indefinite anticoagulation post-VTE in PV (ongoing thrombotic risk).
Target INR 2.0-3.0; 2.5-3.5 for recurrent VTE or splanchnic thrombosis.
DOACs (rivaroxaban, apixaban) increasingly used off-label in MPN VTE;
warfarin modelled here for established RxNorm/NDC availability.
Duration 50 years = lifelong intent.
Any thrombotic event upgrades to high-risk, mandating cytoreduction.
Post-thrombosis cytoreduction check:
Already on HU: consider switch to ruxolitinib
Already on peg-IFN: continue (adequate cytoreduction)
No cytoreduction: initiate HU
Initiating HU post-thrombotic event in previously untreated patient.
Post-thrombosis on HU: consider switch to ruxolitinib.
RESPONSE trial: ruxolitinib superior to BAT for Hct control and spleen reduction.
~50% probability of switching in this scenario.
Discontinue HU before starting ruxolitinib.
Gradual taper recommended to avoid rebound leukocytosis.
RxNorm: 1373464 - Ruxolitinib 5 MG Oral Tablet.
FDA-approved for HU-resistant/intolerant PV (December 2014).
Starting dose PV: 10 mg BID = 2 x 5mg tablets twice daily (amount:2 frequency:2).
RESPONSE trial: hematocrit control 60% vs 20%; primary endpoint 21% vs 1%.
Adverse effects: anaemia, thrombocytopenia, herpes zoster reactivation,
non-melanoma skin cancer (long-term monitoring required).
HU resistance/intolerance: ~15-25% of patients at 5 years.
ELN 2011 resistance criteria: need for phlebotomy (Hct >=45%), PLT >400,
WBC >10 despite >=2g/day HU; failure to reduce splenomegaly >=50%;
Grade 3/4 non-haematologic toxicity at any dose.
Second-line options: ruxolitinib (50%), busulfan (elderly; 30%), or continue/defer (20%).
RxNorm: 1860384 - Busulfan 2 MG Oral Tablet.
Second-line cytoreduction; preferred in elderly patients intolerant of HU.
Induction: 4-6 mg/day until response; maintenance 2-4 mg/day or pulsed.
amount:2 frequency:1 = 4mg/day (induction range lower end).
Effective and well-tolerated in elderly PV; secondary leukaemia risk lower
than historically thought at standard therapeutic doses.
FIX 3: SNOMED: 109962001 - Post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis (disorder).
[v1 used 307561004, which is ambiguous in current SNOMED releases]
Post-PV MF in ~10-20% of patients by 20 years.
IWG-MRT diagnostic criteria:
- Prior documented PV diagnosis
- Bone marrow fibrosis grade MF-2 or MF-3
- >=2 of: anaemia, leukoerythroblastic film, splenomegaly >=5cm,
constitutional symptoms (weight loss >10%, night sweats, fever >37.5C)
Management: ruxolitinib (symptom/splenomegaly control) ± allogeneic SCT.
FIX 13: SCT age-gated to patients <70 years.
Patients >=70: ruxolitinib or supportive care only.
Patients <70: ruxolitinib (65%), SCT evaluation (15%), supportive care (20%).
Paroxetine 20 mg/day for refractory PV-associated pruritus.
Patients <70 eligible for SCT evaluation if DIPSS-plus intermediate-2 or high-risk.
~15% of eligible younger patients proceed to transplant evaluation.
5-year OS with allogenic SCT: ~30-50% with modern conditioning.
Ruxolitinib for symptomatic post-PV MF (splenomegaly, constitutional symptoms).
MF dosing by platelet count: PLT >200: 20mg BID; PLT 100-200: 15mg BID; PLT 50-100: 5mg BID.
amount:4 frequency:2 = 4 x 5mg tablets twice daily = 20mg BID (PLT >200 starting dose).

Risk factors: prior alkylating agents, leukocytosis, SRSF2/IDH2/TP53 mutations.
Median OS post-transformation: 2-5 months.
HU-associated AML risk is low at standard therapeutic doses.
AML from PV: poor prognosis. Intensive 7+3 induction ± allogeneic SCT.
Many patients ineligible due to age/comorbidities; best supportive care.
